title: Redwood x CosmosGPU Partner Intro & Discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery call. High-level alignment on go-to-market and technical fit for Redwood inference runtime on CosmosGPU infrastructure. Key topics: deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), GPU families (A100/H100), networking (VPC peering, private link), security/compliance (SOC2, KMS), pilot scope and benchmarking. Agreed next steps include sharing partner collateral, security questionnaire, and scheduling a technical deep dive / benchmark run in two weeks.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Partnerships), Alec (CosmosGPU Head of Partnerships), Sara (CosmosGPU Director), Devon (CosmosGPU SA)

Summary / Notes (auto): Intro, high-level platform fit, security flags, pilot ask.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): hey everyone thanks for joining we'll give a quick 10 min intro from redwood then we'd love to hear about cosmosgpu and where you see potential to partner, ok?
00:12 Speaker 2 (Alec): yeah thanks maya appreciate it. im a bit hung up from meetings so i'll be short. we run global gpu infra focused on enterprise POCs and managed clusters, trying to expand partner network for inference runtimes.
00:28 Speaker 3 (Jonas): awesome. quick intro, I'm jonas se on infra integrations - we focus on serving runtime, batching, and private deploys, ideally want to make it easy for your customers to run models on cosmoshw.
00:42 Speaker 1 (Maya): quick context on redwood - developer-first inference platform, hosted api + dedicated pools + private/vpc options. our primary pie use-cases are prod llm inference: chat, embeddings, reranking.
00:58 Speaker 2 (Devon): can you remind me what your dedicated offering looks like? we have some customers that want reserved pools with guaranteed throughput.
01:10 Speaker 3 (Jonas): sure reserved capacity is how we call Dedicated - you can reserve GPU pools, autoscale policies, and control placement. we support on-prem / vpc deployments as well if customers need private control plane.
01:24 Speaker 4 (Sara): what's the typical gpu families you run on? we primarily offer a100 and h100 nodes but also have upcoming ga on bf16 optimized hw.
01:36 Speaker 3 (Jonas): we optimize for a100/h100; our runtime picks kernels by arch and seq-length distribution. we do quantization friendly paths too (int8/4bit) - important for cost.
01:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): quick commercial note: for partners we do co-sell/co-market and can support referral credits, we want to understand overlap of customers.
02:05 Speaker 2 (Alec): yeah we see lots of opportunity in mid-market saas and platform teams - some are sensitive to PII and need private deployments.
02:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): perfect that's an ideal fit. can i ask about your onboarding timeline / sales cycle typically?
02:30 Speaker 2 (Alec): typically 3-6 months for enterprise buys; POC stage 2-6 weeks. regions: eu & us primary, apac smaller but growing.
02:43 Speaker 3 (Jonas): for pilot benchmarking - do you have a standard benchmarking harness or would you prefer we bring ours?
02:54 Speaker 2 (Alec): we've got an internal perf harness but we can run yours too. we'd like to validate latency and unit cost numbers.
03:06 Speaker 1 (Maya): great - our SE can provide a lightweight benchmark script that exercises streaming, KV cache and batching. we'll target an 8k token mix and comparative runs on a100/h100.
03:22 Speaker 4 (Sara): security and compliance - we need to know third-party providers' controls. do you have SOC2? encryption at rest? kms?
03:34 Speaker 3 (Jonas): we are SOC2 compliant, support KMS integrations and HSM for private deployments. for Dedicated we can provide audit logs and token level traces via the console.
03:48 Speaker 2 (Devon): how do you handle network connectivity for private deploys? vpc peering, private link?
03:58 Speaker 3 (Jonas): we support VPC peering and private link. for on-prem we can do an appliance model with a customer controlled control plane. sometimes the naming in our docs gets swapped - e.g., 'Private' can look like 'VPC' in some pages.
04:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): (small laugh) right, docs are a work in progress.
04:18 Speaker 5 (Alec): pricing - do you have partner discounts or commit models? enterprise customers are sensitive to predictable unit economics.
04:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved monthly/annual commit. for partners we can discuss referral credits and joint pricing for pilots. we'll follow up with a partner commercial template.
04:41 Speaker 6 (Sara): any known customers running redwood on cloud partners like us? references?
04:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): we have a few partners running dedicated on third-party infra; i can share anonymized case studies.
04:58 Speaker 2 (Devon): technical deep dive question: how do you manage kv-cache across shards when using large context? does your runtime handle cross-node attention?
05:12 Speaker 3 (Jonas): good question - we maintain KV cache per serving instance and our compiler/runtime will co-locate or shard based on model and sequence length. for cross-node we currently fallback to model variants optimized for streaming to avoid cross-host latencies - it's a tradeoff.
05:34 Speaker 1 (Maya): are there any hard constraints we should know about for your container / orchestration for private installs?
05:44 Speaker 3 (Jonas): we can run in k8s or as baremetal docker. for air-gapped customers we hand over a tarball and scripts for install; infra team usually needs around 200GB of image layer data for the runtime and a small operator.
05:58 Speaker 2 (Alec): what about telemetry - does your platform send usage back to redwood? customers ask about data residency.
06:10 Speaker 3 (Jonas): for private deployments telemetry is optional and can be configured to send only health metrics or be completely offline; audit logs can be exported to customer's SIEM.
06:22 Speaker 1 (Maya): perfect. pivoting a bit to GTM - we see partner motion in two patterns: 1) sell-through to your customers where you offer redwood as a managed runtime, 2) co-managed where both sell jointly. which makes more sense for cosmosgpu?
06:38 Speaker 2 (Alec): likely a mix. for enterprise we prefer sell-with/co-sell; for small customers maybe a marketplace listing.
06:47 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok makes sense. for onboarding, who from your side would own technical validation?
06:55 Speaker 2 (Alec): devon will lead tech validation, sara will own commercial / GTM, i'll own partner ops.
07:04 Speaker 3 (Jonas): great devon - jonas here, i'll coordinate the benchmark plan with you.
07:10 Speaker 5 (Devon): noted. what are the success criteria for a pilot?
07:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): typically: 1) meet latency SLOs for targeted models (e.g., 95th < 200ms for short-chat configs), 2) validate unit cost improvements with batching/quantization, 3) integration w/ your network and IAM, 4) basic QA on outputs for few-shot prompts.
07:38 Speaker 6 (Sara): we'd need a partner contract template and an nda for reference architectures.
07:46 Speaker 1 (Maya): we have standard MSA/partner addendum and an NDA template, will share.
07:52 Speaker 5 (Alec): technical risk - we have some customers with strict FIPS/KMS requirements, can you support HSM-backed keys?
08:02 Speaker 3 (Jonas): yes HSM support for Private installs, for hosted we can integrate with customer KMS via private link in some cases. would require contract addendum for key custody.
08:16 Speaker 2 (Devon): any performance numbers you can share on H100 vs A100 for medium models?
08:25 Speaker 3 (Jonas): rough numbers in our notes: H100 often gives 20-40% perf uplift on float workloads and better throughput with bv4/quant paths - but we should benchmark on your hardware to be sure.
08:38 Speaker 1 (Maya): want to do a quick sketch of the pilot timeline?
08:44 Speaker 2 (Alec): sure, ideally pilot run window 2-4 weeks; discovery and planning 1 week; benchmark execution 1 week; analysis and follow-up 1 week. so roughly 4-6 weeks end-to-end.
08:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): sounds good. who will provide the tenant and access for initial runs?
09:04 Speaker 2 (Alec): cosmos can stand up a small dedicated pool in the us-east region; we'll provide creds to devon and your se via a secure method.
09:16 Speaker 3 (Jonas): perfect - we'll need region, instance types, and network details.
09:24 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll also need a small sample dataset and expected traffic pattern.
09:30 Speaker 6 (Sara): ok i'll compile that and send over.
09:36 Speaker 1 (Maya): any outstanding blockers?
09:39 Speaker 2 (Alec): none right now, main thing is clarifying security and contract.
09:42 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok recap - actions: we'll send partner deck + security questionnaire; cosmosgpu will send capacity matrix and compliance contact; schedule technical deep dive and benchmark for week of 2026-03-23.
09:58 Speaker 3 (Jonas): i'll prepare the benchmark harness and a small runbook.
10:04 Speaker 1 (Maya): and we'll loop in biz-dev for co-marketing. thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email.

(End of meeting)
